chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī said: Abu Najīh al-Mismāʿī narrated to me from al-Fayḍ ibn al-Mukhtār.

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! What do you say regarding a land I lease from the Sultan, then I rent it out to my lessees upon a stipulation that whatever Allah brings out from it of anything, the half and the third of that is for me, after the right of the Sultan?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. That is how I deal with my lessees.'

key_terms.أُؤَاجِرُهَا: I rent it out / I lease it
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sub-leasing land leased from the government with a share of the produce?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* establishes the jurisprudential validity of agricultural tenancy contracts (*Ijara*) where the lessee retains a share of the produce after fulfilling state taxes, reflecting the economic practices of the early Shia community under Abbasid rule. Imam al-Sadiq’s affirmation that this mirrors his own dealings with his tenants underscores the practical application of flexible commercial jurisprudence (*Fiqh al-Mu'amalat*) in managing land resources and ensuring equitable profit distribution.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami who said, ‘Abu Najeeh Al Mimai narrated to me from Al Qayz Bin Al Mukhtar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a land I lease from the Sultan (ruling authority), then I rent it out to my lessees upon a stipulation that whatever Allah<sup>ajwj</sup> Brings out from it from anything, what would be for me from that is the half, and the third, after the right (land tax) of the Sultan?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. That is how I<sup>asws</sup> deal with my<sup>asws</sup> lessees’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy who has said that narrated to him abu Najih al-Misma‘iy from al-Fayd ibn al-Mukhtar

who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, what do you say about a land that I rent from al-Sultan, then rent it to my tenants for, whatever Allah makes to grow, one-half or one-third after excluding the share of al-Sultan. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful and that is how I deal with my tenants.’”
